ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening against the FINTRAC politically exposed persons (PEP) framework, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctions lists required by Stripe and Shopify Payments, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the Canadian sanctions regimes under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and applicable provincial securities commission enforcement lists. The cosplay apparel manufacturer is not itself a PCMLTFA reporting entity, but payment service providers (Stripe, Shopify Payments) will impose beneficial-ownership attestations, PEP/sanctions filters, and enhanced due diligence at onboarding, creating a de facto compliance standard.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search), administered by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) and provincial registrars; Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre for federal name reservations; ServiceOntario Ontario Business Registry for the Limited Partnership's provincial registration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of a Canadian Limited Partnership must be expressed in English or French. A business name in a non-official script (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic, or Arabic) must be transliterated into Latin characters and separately searched through NUANS. The statutory suffix must include 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', 'Société en commandite', or 'S.E.N.C.' as required by the provincial Limited Partnerships Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Extension: federal and most provincial name reservations may be renewed before expiry by filing an extension request and paying the prescribed fee; Ontario name reservations are valid for 90 days and are not administratively extended. Rejection appeal: within 21 to 30 days of the written refusal, file a formal reconsideration with the provincial Registrar (or the federal Director under the CBCA) attaching the NUANS report, a legal opinion on distinctiveness, and either the written consent of the conflicting name holder or evidence of acquired goodwill. If the reconsideration is denied, judicial review may be commenced in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice (or the Federal Court for federal names) within 30 days of the final decision, or an administrative appeal may be filed where the provincial statute expressly provides one.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with caveats. Ontario and most common-law provinces accept a virtual executive suite or commercial registered-agent address as the LP's registered office, provided it is a physical street address capable of receiving service of process. However, the general partner must maintain genuine decision-making substance in Canada, and the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) may disregard a purely virtual address when determining the principal establishment for GST/HST registration and provincial tax nexus.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk: approximately 3% to 5% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection for a low-risk cosplay/prop apparel manufacturer operating as an e-commerce retailer. CRA tax auditors, provincial employment/occupational health and safety inspectors, and municipal business-licensing authorities retain the right of unannounced entry, with materially higher inspection probability if the operation stores inventory at a third-party or home-based fulfilment centre.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada has no federal limited partnership statute. Formation is effected under provincial limited partnership legislation; for a cross-provincial footprint the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.7, ss. 2, 9-12 and the Extra-Provincial Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. E.27, s. 3 are the governing statutes.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch, operating through the Ontario Business Registry (ServiceOntario); federal business number issued by the Canada Revenue Agency.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form 1) under the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act; Extra-Provincial Limited Partnership Registration where the limited partnership carries on business outside Ontario.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a limited partnership. Capital contributions may be in cash, property, or services and must be recorded in the partnership agreement. No escrow or trust account is required, but contributed capital must be separately tracked to preserve limited liability status.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner of [LP NAME] hereby accepts the initial subscription of limited partnership units set forth in the Subscription Schedule accompanying this resolution and authorizes the execution of the amended limited partnership agreement. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the limited partnership be established at the address stated in the Declaration and that any change shall require approval of the General Partner. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [INSERT NAME] is appointed as filing agent and chief compliance officer with authority to file the Declaration of Limited Partnership, obtain the Canada Revenue Agency business number, and open the partnership's bank account. FURTHER RESOLVED, that all corporate governance matters proceed in accordance with the limited partnership agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Conduct NUANS Name Search and Reserve the Limited Partnership Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada / Ontario Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search for the proposed limited partnership name and file a name reservation request with the Ontario Business Registry. Submit the request online or through a service provider; if the partnering jurisdiction requires a federal trademark search, include that search as part of the preliminary clearance.
required_dossiers: Authorization letter from the proposed general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because of similarity to an existing registered name, file an alternative name with a revised NUANS report. No fee is refunded; a new reservation request and fee are required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel instructed by the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement in accordance with the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act. The agreement must set out the name, registered office, general partner identity, capital contributions, profit-sharing percentages, management powers, withdrawal provisions, and the limitation on limited partner participation in management. Ensure the agreement is executed by all initial partners and notarized if any partner is located outside Canada.
required_dossiers: Consent of all general and limited partners
Notarized certified copies for foreign partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The limited partnership agreement is not filed with the registry. If a defect is identified, amend the agreement by written consent of all partners and restate the relevant capital and management clauses before filing the Declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form 1, Declaration of Limited Partnership, to the Ontario Business Registry. Provide the reserved name, registered office address in Ontario, the name and address of each general partner, and the amount contributed by each limited partner as stated in the partnership agreement. Pay the applicable filing fee and upload the executed partnership agreement if requested. Retain the registry-issued certificate as proof of formation.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office address in Ontario
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Declaration is queried or rejected, correct the noted deficiencies and refile the Declaration within 10 business days. Cure any clerical errors in the registered office address or general partner identification and submit an amended Declaration with a further fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Extra-Provincially in Other Provinces of Operation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Each provincial corporate registry, including Alberta Corporate Registry and BC Corporate Online, as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the limited partnership will carry on business in provinces other than Ontario, file an Extra-Provincial Limited Partnership Registration in each such province. Appoint an attorney for service in each province and submit a certified copy of the Ontario Declaration together with the prescribed provincial registration forms. Confirm local zoning approvals for any physical manufacturing site before filing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Ontario Declaration of Limited Partnership
Power of attorney appointing an attorney for service in each province
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an extra-provincial registration is rejected for an invalid attorney for service or incomplete certified documents, correct the appointment and refile with the provincial registry. Late registrations may attract penalties; remedy by paying the late fee and filing an updated registrant statement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Federal Business Number and Tax Program Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership with the Canada Revenue Agency to obtain a federal business number, GST/HST account, and, if employees will be hired, a payroll deduction account and WSIB registration. If the partnership will import or export costume fabric, props, wigs, or finished apparel, also apply for the CRA import/export program account and the relevant customs carrier code. Open a partnership bank account after receiving the business number.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Declaration of Limited Partnership
Government-issued identification for the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the partnership's existence or the general partner's authority, provide the Declaration, partnership agreement, and an updated Statement of Partners. File a T5013 Supplementary Information Return if the partnership is required to file for the income tax year, and remedy any late instalment penalty by paying the assessed amount and filing the corrected schedule.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable at federal level; municipal building and zoning departments issue physical occupancy permits for the manufacturing site.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No federal industrial manufacturing licence is required for ISIC 3240 costume apparel, prop apparel, and synthetic wig production under the current Canada federal regulatory regime.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada, with the applicable provincial environmental ministry such as the Ontario Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is required for low-impact garment cutting, sewing, and wig manufacturing. The activity is not listed on the Federal List of Toxic Substances and is not otherwise prescribed for a federal EIA under the Impact Assessment Act; a self-registration checklist is recommended for waste and wastewater discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to municipal sanitary sewers must comply with the local sewer-use by-law limits for pH, oil and grease, and suspended solids. VOC emissions from adhesives or coatings must remain below thresholds listed under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999, and any textile waste containing synthetic polymers must be disposed of as industrial solid waste under provincial waste management rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire safety inspection and fire code certificate are required for the manufacturing premises. Structural load inspection is required for storage racks and mezzanines. Occupational health and safety clearance must be obtained through the workplace safety regulator in the province of operation, and the business must register with the applicable workers' compensation authority before commencing production.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); registration portal: Business Registration Online (BRO); compliance portal: My Business Account (GST/HST).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Canadian-resident limited partnership (LP) must obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN) from the CRA. Register through BRO (online) or by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number). The BN is issued at the partnership level; the LP then opens a GST/HST account under the same BN. For non-resident owners, the LP may register as a non-resident registrant using CRA Form RC1 with Form RC459 (GST/HST Non-Resident Registration), or apply online where the designated partner holds valid Canadian identification. Voluntary registration under ETA s. 240(3) is permitted before the threshold is reached to recover input tax credits (ITCs) on startup and pre-revenue costs. The LP file a T5013 Summary and T5013 slips for each fiscal period; the BN is referenced in all returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. The LP is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes (ITA ss. 96–103): the partnership itself pays no federal income tax; income, gains, losses and credits flow through to partners pro rata under the partnership agreement. The LP is a Canadian partnership if it is established under provincial law (e.g., Ontario Limited Partnerships Act) and carries on business in Canada; its partners are taxed on worldwide income if Canadian-resident. Non-resident partners are taxable on Canadian-source income from the partnership and may be subject to Part XIII withholding (25%) on distributions of other income. For GST/HST, the partnership is nevertheless a separate 'person' (ETA s. 48) requiring its own registration. No federal tax-exempt zone applies to cosplay prop apparel manufacturing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style 'check-the-box' election exists; classification follows juridical form and CRA administrative position. Available elections: (1) Voluntary GST/HST registration (ETA s. 240(3)); (2) Partnership fiscal-period election (ITA s. 249.1(8)) permitting a non-calendar taxation year where no corporation holds a majority partnership interest; (3) Hybrid-mismatch timing and allocation election under ITA ss. 18.4–18.6 to neutralize deduction/non-inclusion differences involving non-resident partners; (4) Election under ITA s. 96(1) to compute income at the partnership level in Canadian currency; (5) Net-filing election to use GST/HST NETFILE. For non-resident partners, an election under Part XIII can be made to file a corporate tax return instead of withholding (where applicable).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) under the Excise Tax Act (Part IX).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000: total value of taxable supplies (including zero-rated exports) made in Canada by the LP and its associates in the current calendar quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (ETA s. 148(1)). Exceeding this threshold makes GST/HST registration mandatory; below it, registration is voluntary.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, no digital stamping, and no mandatory API-based invoice authorization. Business invoices must meet ETA s. 169 and Regulation 238 (information content), and may be issued and stored electronically. PEPPOL-based e-invoicing is voluntary. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically via CRA GST/HST NETFILE, GSTR, or an accredited service provider once annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 1.5 million. Payment rails (Stripe, Shopify Payments) must collect GST at the point of sale and remit through the LP's GST/HST account; no separate fiscal clearance API is prescribed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: COSPLAY APPAREIL EXPORT: Finished goods (synthetic wigs, costume robes, props) sold to non-resident purchasers and exported by the LP qualify for 0% GST under ETA Sched. VI, Part V, s. 2 (goods exported by the supplier) and s. 1 (goods delivered to a residence outside Canada pursuant to the supply). Services performed entirely outside Canada (e.g., pattern licensing, offshore design) are zero-rated under Part V, s. 7. To claim 0%, the LP must show that the goods were exported 'as soon as is reasonably possible' after sale and must retain the required documentation. Zero-rated supplies retain full ITC eligibility.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Reporting: Canadian Export Declaration via CAED (Canadian Automated Export Declaration) or carrier e-manifest for shipments valued at CAD 2,000 or more; low-value shipments evidenced by courier waybill
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / Express Courier Waybill showing consignee address outside Canada
Commercial Invoice with HS classification (e.g., HS 6114, 6704, 9505), original value, and stated 0% GST

Proof of Foreign Exchange Settlement: bank statement, SWIFT MT103, or Stripe/Shopify settlement record evidencing receipt of funds from the foreign purchaser (functional equivalent of an inward remittance certificate; Canadian banks do not issue 'inward remittance certificates' as a standard product)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds repatriation deadline; however, CRA audit practice treats settlement delays beyond 180 days as raising substantive doubt on the export sale, potentially triggering a reassessment to remove zero-rating. Assessment window: generally 4 years from filing (ETA s. 298(2)); extended to 10 years+ for misrepresentation or fraud. Reassessed GST (full 5%) is clawed back with arrears interest (ETA s. 280). Penalties: ETA s. 281.1(1) imposes a minimum CAD 250 plus 25% of the avoided tax for false statements made knowingly or under gross negligence; criminal evasion under ETA s. 327 carries fines of 50%–200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years. Under ETA s. 272.1, every partner is jointly and severally liable for the LP's GST/HST debts, including clawbacks and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); with exchange-control authority historically vested in the Minister of Finance and no separate Foreign Exchange Control Board; cross-border AML oversight by FINTRAC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital accounts. Canada is an IMF Article VIII jurisdiction; no approval is required for profit remittances, distribution of partnership earnings, or capital repatriation. Non-resident limited partners are subject to Part XIII withholding tax on distributions, with treaty relief available; CAD floats freely with no surrender or conversion obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts in Canada. Exporters must retain commercial documentation for CBSA/Statistics Canada reporting and file the Canadian Export Declaration (via Canadian Export Reporting System) for controlled goods and goods exceeding listed thresholds. All cross-border EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more are reportable to FINTRAC.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with merchant acquiring integration
Operational Account plus cross-border USD clearing
Operational Account with trade finance desk
Operational Account with FX hedging line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. FINTRAC-registered money services businesses (e.g., Wise Platform, Payoneer, Airwallex) can support low-value marketplace payouts and USD/EUR/CNY supplier disbursements, but they cannot serve as the primary treasury anchor. Since 2024, the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) subjects independent payment service providers to Bank of Canada and Consumer Protection supervision; such fintech rails are restricted from offering Canadian deposit accounts, lending, or credit facilities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted for Canadian-domiciled entities via e-signature and video-verified identity checks; no physical branch attendance is statutorily mandated. However, if any limited partner is non-resident, the Schedule I bank may impose enhanced due diligence requiring a notarized partnership resolution, a Canadian registered agent confirmation, or a video interview with the general partner. The LP can satisfy such requirements entirely from the documentary dossier without a physical visit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial-owner opacity in a multi-layer limited partnership structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete partnership agreement, general partner resolution, current organizational chart with full ownership chain, beneficial-ownership declaration identifying each limited partner, source-of-wealth letters, passport copies, and a sworn declaration of non-money-laundering purposes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity, low-value settlement flows from Stripe and Shopify Payments flagged as unjustified merchant volume
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly marketplace payout statements, GST/HST and provincial sales tax returns, platform terms-of-service agreements, refund and chargeback policies, supplier purchase invoices, and reviewed annual financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash concentration from in-person cosplay convention and event sales
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Point-of-sale terminal transaction logs, daily sales reconciliation sheets, cash deposit slips, event venue concession agreements, and inventory reconciliation reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IP or trademark infringement suspicion on licensed theatrical costume reproductions and prop accessories
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Non-infringement legal opinion, design originality memoranda, license agreements if third-party IP is lawfully used, model releases for photographic marketing, and a compliant takedown/cease-and-desist log.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from foreign limited partners must be routed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code CAPI (capital contributions) and field 70 remittance information identifying the partnership and dated capital contribution notice. Canada imposes no exchange-control approval step; the receiving Schedule I bank will require the LP's institution, transit, and account numbers. Inbound transfers of CAD 10,000 or more trigger FINTRAC EFT reporting and should be pre-notified with a treasury deposit schedule to ensure same-day ledger matching.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlement for cosplay fabrics, synthetic wig fibers, and prop components is executed primarily through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for subordinate amounts and documentary collections (sight L/C) for large bulk orders from Asia. Domestic disbursements use Interac e-Transfer and bank-direct payroll clearing; low-value cross-border payouts to international artisans and marketplace refunds can be cleared via Wise or Currencycloud API rails. All outbound wires require recording of purpose codes in compliance with CBSA Statistics Canada export data and FINTRAC reporting above CAD 10,000.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD spot and forward contracts (tenor up to 24 months) with a Schedule I counterparty
Vanilla FX options on USD/CAD, EUR/CAD, and CNY/CAD
Non-deliverable forwards for restricted third-currency exposures only; CAD/USD NDFs are unnecessary given full convertibility

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Limited Partnership Annual Declaration (registry renewal) with updated registered office and partner particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial corporate/partnership registry of the province of registration (primary jurisdiction); extra-provincial registries in each Canadian province where the LP carries on business
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 60 days after the LP's fiscal year-end in fiscal-year registries (calendar-year LP: March 1) or on the registration anniversary in anniversary-date registries
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Provincial fines up to CAD 200 for late declaration; two consecutive years of non-filing trigger administrative dissolution (strike-off); reinstatement requires payment of arrears, penalties, and registry discretion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (income tax information return of the limited partnership)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end; within 5 months after the fiscal year-end for non-calendar fiscal periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per limited partner per month up to 24 months (maximum CAD 2,500 per 12-month period; 25% escalation for repeat non-filing); continued 24-month default may trigger CRA administrative measures including deemed cessation of the partnership

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end for annual GST/HST filers (taxable supplies under CAD 1.5M); monthly and quarterly filers file within 1 month after each reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 1% of the balance due plus interest, increasing to 6% when an arrears balance exists; sustained non-filing leads to refund suppression and possible prosecution for willful evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation (individuals with significant control over the LP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial corporate/partnership registry (beneficial ownership transparency register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the LP Annual Declaration; updated filing within 15 days of any limited partnership interest transfer or change in significant control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties up to CAD 5,000 for individuals and CAD 25,000 for entities per infraction; refusal to correct the register can block registry filings and trigger prosecution under provincial transparency legislation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit is imposed by the Canada Partnerships Act or provincial Limited Partnerships Acts; audit becomes mandatory only when (i) the LP is a reporting issuer under provincial securities laws, (ii) total annual gross revenue exceeds CAD 20M and the partnership agreement demands verified financials, or (iii) the partnership agreement or lender covenants require certified statements; small private LPs may waive the audit by unanimous partner resolution
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) for publicly accountable and reporting-issuer LPs; Canadian ASPE (Part II) for private LPs; financial statements must accompany the T5013 schedules and be prepared consistently with the chosen framework

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation required in connection with the annual declaration: the LP must verify and re-file beneficial ownership data (individuals with significant control, 25% direct or indirect threshold) every year, and file a change notice within 15 days of any transfer of limited partnership interests; non-resident limited partners above the threshold are included
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of the General Partner (incorporating resolutions)
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (UBO Register)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% (federal general corporate rate under ITA s.123; limited partnership is fiscally transparent, so the partner-level rate applies)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying Canadian manufacturing and processing profits are subject to the reduced 13% federal M&P rate (2% M&P deduction); a Canadian-controlled private corporate partner may claim the small business deduction on its share of active business income up to CAD 500,000, producing a 9% federal rate; SR&ED investment tax credits up to 35% refundable for CCPCs and accelerated CCA for eligible manufacturing equipment further reduce the effective federal burden.
